sources.name: Aalto Dictionary of Machine Learning (ADictML), Alexander Jung and contributors
sources.changes: first sentence of each definition, LaTeX converted to plain text

entries.short: The output of an artificial neuron within an artificial neural network is referred to as its activation.
AdaBoost is a specific boosting algorithm that combines base learners sequentially.
An agent denotes any system that implements some form of online learning.
An algorithm is a precise, step-by-step specification for producing an output from a given input within a finite number of well-defined computational steps.
The ADMM is an iterative optimization method for solving a structured optimization problem.
An API is a formal mechanism that allows software components to interact in a structured and modular way.
An application programming interface endpoint is a specific address within an application programming interface at which a particular function or resource can be accessed.
The AUC is a quantitative measure of the usefulness of a binary classifier.
AI refers to systems that behave rationally, in the sense of maximizing a long-term reward.
An ANN is a graphical (signal-flow) representation of a hypothesis that maps features of a data point at its input to a prediction for the corresponding label at its output.
An artificial neuron is the basic building block of an artificial neural network.
An attack on a machine learning system refers to an intentional action—either active or passive—that compromises the system's integrity, availability, or confidentiality.
The augmented Lagrangian is a modification of the standard Lagrangian that includes an additional quadratic penalty term for constraint violations.
An automaton is a mathematical representation of a computing device whose behavior is described by a set of internal states, a memory structure, and a state-transition rule.
A backdoor attack refers to the intentional manipulation of a machine learning training process.
A base learner is a machine learning method that is part of an ensemble method.
In the context of stochastic gradient descent, a batch refers to a randomly chosen subset of the overall training set.
In batch learning (also known as offline learning), the machine learning model is trained on the entire dataset in a single training iteration, instead of updating it incrementally as data arrive.
Consider a probabilistic model for a machine learning application where each data point is interpreted as a random variable.
Binary classification refers to classification with two labels.
The BCE loss is a special case of cross-entropy loss for a binary classification problem.
Boosting is an iterative optimization method to learn an accurate hypothesis map (or strong learner) by sequentially combining less accurate base learners (referred to as weak learners).
The Brier score evaluates probabilistic predictions for binary outcomes.
In a distributed machine learning system, a Byzantine device is one that deviates arbitrarily from its prescribed behavior.
In the context of machine learning, causality refers to cause–effect relationships between quantities, such as the features and labels of data points.
A checkpoint is a saved representation of the state of a running computation.
Checkpointing is a fault-tolerance mechanism that periodically creates checkpoints by saving the state of a running computation to persistent storage.
The Chernoff bound is a concentration inequality derived as a direct application of Markov's inequality.
Cloud computing is a computing paradigm in which computational resources such as processing, storage, and networking are provided as on-demand services over a communication network.
A cluster is a subset of data points that are more similar to each other than to the data points outside the cluster.
Clustering methods decompose a given dataset into a few clusters.
CFL trains local models for the devices in a federated learning application by using a clustering assumption, i.e., the devices of a federated learning network form clusters.
Clustering methods decompose a given set of data points into a few subsets, which are referred to as clusters.
The clustering assumption postulates that data points in a dataset form a (small) number of groups or clusters.
Consider a clustering method that decomposes a given dataset into clusters.
A communication network is a collection of devices interconnected by communication links that allow them to exchange information.
By computational aspects of a machine learning method, we mainly refer to the computational resources required for its implementation.
Concentration inequality refers to an upper bound on the probability that a random variable deviates more than a prescribed amount from its expectation.
Consider a deep net, consisting of several hidden layers, trained to predict the label of a data point from its feature vector.
The conjugate transpose of a matrix is obtained by transposing the matrix and taking the complex conjugate of each entry.
A constrained optimization problem is an optimization problem that involves constraints on the optimization variable.
Convex optimization studies the formulation, properties, and efficient solution methods for convex optimization problems.
A coreset is a small subset of a larger dataset that approximates certain properties of the original dataset.
A covariance function characterizes the second-order dependence structure of a stochastic process.
Cross-sectional data consist of data points whose attributes are measured once, without explicitly modeling temporal evolution.
In the context of machine learning, the term data is often used as a synonym for dataset.
Data augmentation methods add synthetic data points to an existing set of data points.
European data protection regulation includes a data minimization principle.
Data normalization refers to transformations applied to the feature vectors of data points to improve the machine learning method's statistical aspects or computational aspects.
Data parallelism refers to a widely used class of distributed optimization methods for training a machine learning model.
A data point is any object that conveys information.
Data poisoning refers to the intentional manipulation (or fabrication) of data points to maliciously steer the training of a machine learning model.
A dataset is a set of distinct data points.
A deep net is an artificial neural network with a (relatively) large number of hidden layers.
Degree of belonging is a number that indicates the extent to which a data point belongs to a cluster.

A denoising autoencoder extends the basic autoencoder by perturbing (e.g., by intentionally adding noise to) the input vector (or feature vector) before feeding it into the autoencoder itself during the training.

entries.term: density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise
entries.short: DBSCAN refers to a clustering algorithm for data points that are characterized by numeric feature vectors.
The term design matrix is a synonym for the feature matrix, particularly used in statistics.
The term device refers to a physical system that can store and process data.
A diffusion method is a generative machine learning method that trains a model to approximate the reversal of a gradual stochastic corruption process.
A DAG is a directed graph that contains no directed cycles.
A directed graph contains edges that have an orientation (or direction).
The distance between two points in a metric space is the value of the metric evaluated at those points.
A distributed algorithm is an algorithm designed for a special type of computer, i.e., a collection of interconnected computing devices.
A dynamical system is an abstract system whose output depends on an internal state that evolves over time according to a state-update rule.
Early exit methods refer to computational strategies for evaluating the prediction of a deep net.

Consider an empirical risk minimization-based method that uses an iterative optimization method (such as gradient descent) to learn model parameters by minimizing the empirical risk on a given training set.

Edge computing refers to the placement of computation and data storage close to the sources of data generation, such as sensors, mobile devices, or embedded systems, rather than in centralized data centers.
An edge device operates at or near the edge of a communication network.
Entropy quantifies the uncertainty or unpredictability associated with a random variable.
An environment denotes the external system with which an agent interacts over time.
The EM algorithm is an iterative optimization method for approximately solving certain maximum likelihood optimization problems that are difficult to solve directly.
XML methods aim to complement each prediction with an explanation of how the prediction has been obtained.
One approach to enhance the transparency of a machine learning method for its human user is to provide an explanation alongside the predictions delivered by the method.
A feature of a data point is one of its properties that can be measured or computed easily without the need for human supervision.
The feature space of a given machine learning application or method is constituted by all potential values that the feature vector of a data point can take on.
FedAvg refers to a family of iterative federated learning algorithms.
FedGD refers to a federated learning distributed algorithm that can be implemented as message passing across a federated learning network.
FL is an umbrella term for machine learning methods that train models in a collaborative fashion using decentralized data and computation.
A federated learning network is a mathematical model for a federated learning system that consists of interconnected devices.
A federated learning system is a distributed machine learning system in which multiple computational devices collaborate to train machine learning models without sharing their raw local data.
FedProx refers to an iterative federated learning algorithm that alternates between separately training local models and combining the updated local model parameters.
FedSGD refers to a federated learning distributed algorithm that can be implemented as message passing across a federated learning network.
FedRelax refers to a generalized total variation minimization-based federated learning method for training local models at the devices of a federated learning network.
The FMI is a government agency responsible for gathering and reporting weather data in Finland.
The solution of optimization problems arising in machine learning can often be characterized by a fixed-point equation.
A fixed-point iteration is an iterative method for solving a fixed-point equation, which, in a machine learning context, often arises from an optimization problem.
Generalization refers to the ability of a model trained on a training set to make accurate predictions on new unseen data points.
GTVMin is an instance of regularized empirical risk minimization using the generalized total variation of local model parameters as a regularizer.
A GNN is a special type of artificial neural network that is defined via a given graph.
Hard clustering refers to the task of partitioning a given set of data points into (a few) nonoverlapping clusters.

The high-dimensional regime of empirical risk minimization is characterized by the effective dimension of the model being larger than the sample size, i.e., the number of (labeled) data points in the training set.
The Huber loss unifies the squared error loss and the absolute error loss.
Huber regression refers to empirical risk minimization-based methods that use the Huber loss as a measure of the prediction error.
A hypothesis space is a mathematical model that characterizes the learning capacity of a machine learning method.
Image segmentation refers to the task of clustering the pixels of an image into a few segments.
The independent and identically distributed assumption is a widely used probabilistic model for the generation of data points.
Consider some process that can result in different possible outcomes (e.g., survival or death of a patient).
The infimum of a set of real numbers is the largest number that is less than or equal to every element in the set.
The term input vector is often used as a synonym for the feature vector of a data point.
The elementary computational step during the execution of an algorithm is referred to as iteration.
A label is a higher-level fact or quantity of interest associated with a data point.
In a machine learning application, each data point is described by a set of features together with an associated label.
A labeled data point is a data point whose label is known or has been determined by some means that might require human labor.

The law of large numbers refers to the convergence of the average of an increasing (large) number of independent and identically distributed random variables to the mean of their common probability distribution.
Least absolute deviation regression is an instance of empirical risk minimization using the absolute error loss.

entries.term: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator
entries.short: The Lasso is an instance of explainable empirical risk minimization.
LDA is a classical feature learning method.
Linear least squares refers to the variant of linear regression that uses the squared error loss to measure the quality of a linear hypothesis map.
The concept of a local dataset is in between the concept of a data point and a dataset.
Longitudinal data consist of data points whose attributes are measured repeatedly over time.
MLaaS refers to a cloud computing service model in which machine learning capabilities are provided to users via standardized network interfaces.
The term ML pipeline refers to a composition (i.e., concatenation) of several functions within a machine learning system.
A machine learning system consists of computational devices that can gather and store data, execute algorithms, and exchange information via communication networks.
We use the term map as a synonym for function.
A marginal distribution refers to the probability distribution of a subset of the random variables belonging to a stochastic process.
The term marginalization refers to the process of computing the probability distribution of a subset of random variables from the joint probability distribution of a stochastic process.
An MDP is a mathematical structure for the study of reinforcement learning.
The MAE of a hypothesis is the average absolute error loss computed over a given dataset.
Consider a random experiment, such as recording the air temperature at an Finnish Meteorological Institute weather station.
Consider a machine learning method that learns a hypothesis via empirical risk minimization on a training set.
Message passing is a communication paradigm in which devices exchange information by sending and receiving messages over a network.
A metric is a quantitative measure used to compare objects.
Given a set of real numbers, the minimum is the smallest of those numbers.
Mirror descent is an iterative optimization method obtained by generalizing the gradient step.
Consider a dataset constituted by data points collected via some physical device.
A mobile device is a portable computing device equipped with computational, storage, sensing, and wireless communication capabilities.
The study and design of machine learning methods is often based on a mathematical model.
The MCP is an open specification for the communication between large language model-based aisystems and different data sources.
A model inversion is a form of privacy attack on a machine learning system.
Model parallelism refers to a particular class of distributed optimization methods used to train a machine learning model.
The elements of a parametric model are specified by quantities that are referred to as model parameters.
Model poisoning refers to the intentional manipulation of the training process of a machine learning model.
In machine learning, model selection refers to the process of choosing between different candidate models.
Multi-label classification problems and methods use data points that are characterized by several labels.
An MAB is a precise formulation of a sequential decision-making task under uncertainty.
Multitask learning aims to leverage relations between different learning tasks.
NLP studies machine learning methods for the the analysis and generation of human language.

The network least absolute shrinkage and selection operator is a special case of generalized total variation minimization, obtained by using a norm-based discrepancy measure for comparing local model parameters.
Networked data consist of local datasets that are related by some notion of pairwise similarity.
nExpFam is a collection of exponential families, each of them assigned to a node of a federated learning network.
NFL refers to methods that learn personalized models in a distributed fashion.
We refer to a function as non-smooth if it is not smooth.
Nonparametric machine learning methods do not assume a fixed model structure with a finite number of model parameters.
A norm is a function that maps each (vector) element of a vector space to a nonnegative real number.
See Gaussian random variable, multivariate normal distribution, central limit theorem.

An online algorithm processes input data incrementally, receiving data points sequentially and making decisions or producing outputs (or decisions) immediately without having access to the entire input in advance.
Some machine learning methods are designed to process data in a sequential manner, updating their model parameters one at a time, as new data points become available.
An operator is a function whose domain and co-domain have a specific mathematical structure such as a vector space, a Hilbert space, or a metric space.
See convex optimization, optimization method, optimization problem.
An optimization method is an algorithm that takes a representation of an optimization problem as input and computes an (approximate) solution as its output.
Outcome is one possible result of a physical process.
The term output is sometimes used as a synonym for the label of a data point.
The term output vector is used as a synonym for the label vector of a dataset.
The parameter of a machine learning model is a tunable (i.e., learnable or adjustable) quantity that allows us to choose between different hypothesis maps.
A parametric model is a mathematical model characterized by a finite set of variable quantities called parameters.
The perceptron is one of the oldest machine learning algorithms; it was developed by Frank Rosenblatt in 1957.
Polynomial regression is an instance of empirical risk minimization that learns a polynomial hypothesis map to predict a numeric label based on the numeric features of a data point.
The study and design of machine learning methods is often based on a probabilistic model for the data generation process.
In the probabilistic analysis of a machine learning system, one typically distinguishes between observed data points and unknown parameters of a probabilistic model.
Precision is a metric commonly used in binary classification for the assessment of trained models.
A predictor is a real-valued hypothesis map.
Preprocessing refers to the set of operations applied to raw data before they are fed into a machine learning algorithm.
In the probabilistic analysis of a machine learning system, one typically distinguishes between observed data points and unknown parameters of a probabilistic model.
A privacy attack on a machine learning system aims to infer sensitive attributes of individuals by exploiting partial access to a trained machine learning model.
The privacy funnel is a method for learning a feature map that provides privacy-friendly features for a data point.
A probabilistic model for the generation of data points consists of random variables with a joint probability distribution.
To analyze machine learning methods, it can be useful to interpret data points as independent and identically distributed realizations of a random variable.
A probability space is a mathematical structure that allows us to reason about a random experiment, e.g., the observation of a physical phenomenon.
A convex function for which the proximal operator can be computed efficiently is sometimes referred to as proximable or simple.
A proximal algorithm refers to an optimization method that uses proximal operators as the main computational primitive.
Q-learning is a popular reinforcement learning algorithm that learns an optimal policy by estimating the optimal action-value function (or Q-function).
A random forest is a set of different decision trees.
An RGG is a probabilistic model for graphs built from nodes randomly placed in a metric space.
An RV is a function that maps the outcomes of a random experiment to elements of a measurable space.
Recall is a metric commonly used in binary classification for the assessment of trained models.
Regression problems revolve around the prediction of a numeric label solely from the features of a data point.
See regularized empirical risk minimization.
A relational model is a mathematical representation of data.
The term response is sometimes used as a synonym for the label of a data point.
The term response vector is used as a synonym for the label vector of a dataset.
Robustness is a key requirement for trustAI.
The sample size is the number of individual data points contained in a sample or dataset.
A sample space is the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.
Consider an empirical risk minimization-based method that learns a hypothesis by minimizing the average loss on a training set.
A visualization technique that depicts data points using markers in a 2-D plane.
Self-supervised learning uses some of the features of a data point as its label.
SSL methods use unlabeled data points to support the learning of a hypothesis from labeled data points.
machine learning revolves around learning a hypothesis map that allows us to predict the label of a data point from its features.
Some machine learning applications generate data points that are related by a domain-specific notion of similarity.
Soft clustering refers to the task of partitioning a given set of data points into (a few) overlapping clusters.
An eigenvalue decomposition of a normal matrix is called a spectral decomposition.
A spot instance is a type of cloud computing service that provides computational resources at a reduced cost but without guarantees on availability.
Stacking is one of the main types of ensemble methods.
In a distributed machine learning system (e.g., a federated learning system), staleness refers to the degree to which a copy of model parameters is outdated.

A state is a mathematical representation of the minimal information needed to characterize a system at a given time such that, together with the system dynamics, it suffices to predict the system’s future behavior.
The state space of a system is constituted by all possible states of the system at any point in time.
By statistical aspects of a machine learning method, we refer to (properties of) the probability distribution of its output under a probabilistic model for the data fed into the method.
We refer to a method as stochastic if it involves a random component or is governed by probabilistic laws.
A stochastic algorithm uses a random mechanism during its execution.
A stochastic multiarmed bandit is a stochastic process that is obtained from a multiarmed bandit.
Many machine learning methods use iterative algorithms that construct a sequence of model parameters in order to minimize the training error.
The process of splitting a dataset into subsets, so called strata, according to some key attribute is called stratification.
A stratum is a subset of data points that all share a common property (which could be a feature or a label).
An SCM is a mathematical model of cause–effect relationships underlying a data generation process.
Subgradient descent is a generalization of gradient descent that does not require differentiability of the function to be minimized.
The supremum of a set of real numbers is the smallest number that is greater than or equal to every element in the set.
Tabular data consist of data points that are characterized by a common set of attributes.
The term target is sometimes used as a synonym for the label of a data point.
The term target vector is used as a synonym for the label vector of a dataset.
A test set refers to a set of data points that have been used neither to train a model (e.g., via empirical risk minimization) nor to choose between different models in a validation set.
Training error is the average loss of a hypothesis when predicting the labels of the data points in a training set.
The transpose of a real-valued matrix is obtained by exchanging rows and columns.
An estimator for the parameters of a probabilistic model is unbiased if its expectation equals the true value of the parameters.
In the context of machine learning, uncertainty refers to the presence of multiple plausible outcomes or explanations based on available data.
Consider a machine learning method applying empirical risk minimization to learn a hypothesis that minimizes the empirical risk on a given training set.
A vector is an element of a vector space.
In VFL, different devices have access to different features of the same set of data points.
A weighted graph is a graph whose edges are assigned numeric weights.
Early single-layer artificial neural network.
Type of artificial neural network.
Machine learning technique that attempts to prevent models being fooled by supplying deceptive input.
Device that provides hardware acceleration for artificial intelligence applications.
Concept in artificial intelligence.
Neural network that learns efficient data encoding in an unsupervised manner.
Process of automating the end-to-end process of machine learning.
Computer-based method for shortening a text.
Representation of a type of random process.
Model of text which uses a representation of text that is based on an unordered collection (a "bag") of words.
Artificial neural network.
Non-linear regression method.

Parallel computing paradigm similar to neural networks, with the difference that communication is allowed between neighbouring units only.

Science of extracting information from chemical systems by data-driven means.
Detection of a checkerboard pattern in computer vision.
Mathematical test proposed by Gregory Chow.
Type of artificial neural network.
Form of unsupervised learning in artificial neural networks.
Variation of artificial neural networks that have an architecture whose evolution is guided by genetic algorithms.
Extension of logistic regression that allows one to account for stratification and matching.
Two related tools in statistical analysis.
Artificial neural network based expert systems where the ANN generates inferencing rules e.g., fuzzy-multi layer perceptron where linguistic and natural form of inputs are used.
Particular statistical technique for carrying out a cross-sectional study.
Algorithm that recursively splits data on attributes to build a tree for classification or regression.
Type of artificial neural network.
Artificial neural network with more than one hidden layer.
Techniques combining deep learning and reinforcement learning principles to create efficient machine learning algorithms.
Method of multiple regression analysis used in behavioural genetics.
Computer system intended to converse with a human.
Artificial neural network architecture.
Problem in library science, information science and computer science.
Processing of scanned text document.
Field associated with machine learning and transfer learning.
Class of dynamic neutral networks.
Recurrent neural network with a sparsely connected hidden layer.
Type of computer vision.

Paradigm in machine learning where the entire process from input to output is learned through a single, integrated neural network or a series of interconnected models, in contrast to having independent subsystems.
In machine learning, the use of multiple algorithms to obtain better predictive performance than from any of the constituent learning algorithms alone.
Form of machine learning.
Type of artificial neural network.
Methods for finding parts of an image relevant to a computational task.
A set of techniques that learn a feature: a transformation of raw data input to a representation that can be effectively exploited in machine learning tasks.
Artificial neural network in which connections between the nodes do not form a cycle.
Machine learning approach that enables a system to learn new tasks or recognize new objects from only a few examples or demonstrations.
Method for acquisition of 3d micro topographies.
Special artificial neural network that can handle graphs.

Biological theory of intelligence.
In machine learning, a loss function used for maximum‐margin classification.
Loss function used in robust regression.
Method of machine learning.
In signal processing, a computational method.
Learning programs from data.
Automatically extracting structured information from un- or semi-structured machine-readable documents, such as human language texts.
Technique in statistics.
Type of artificial neural network architecture.
Approximation method in statistics.
Statistical approach for modeling the relationship between a scalar dependent variable and one or more explanatory variables.

Average cross-entropy between the distribution of the true labels and the predictions.
Concept in machine learning.
Learning framework inspired by feed-forward processing in the ventral stream of visual cortex and originally developed for recognition and classification of objects in visual scenes.
Software for understanding biological data.
Applications of machine learning to quantum physics.
Use of machine learning in video games.
Use of software for language translation.
Subfield of machine learning where automatic learning algorithms are applied to metadata about machine learning experiments.
Statistical tool used in meta-analyses.

Form of machine learning where a model learns multiple tasks.
Problem of classifying instances into one of three or more classes.
Statistical regression technique.
Machine learning combining different information resources, such as images and text.
Regression for more than two discrete outcomes.
Type of supervised learning in machine learning.
Machine learning methods that use a predefined set of kernels and learn an optimal linear or non-linear combination of kernels as part of the algorithm.
Non-parametric regression technique.
Automatic text generation using a computer algorithm.
Subtopic of natural language processing in artificial intelligence.
A neural field is a type of neural network that models a mathematical field in a continuous and differentiable way.
Machine learning framework.
Neural network with external memory.
Type of statistical regression analysis.
Summary of algorithms for nonlinear dimensionality reduction.
Estimation method that seeks to fit a curve to a data set, where the mathematical model of the relationship between dependent and independent variables is not linear.
Category of regression analysis.
Computer technology related to computer vision and image processing.
Method of machine learning.
Object categorization problem that aims to learn information about object categories from one training sample.
A method where a model is trained incrementally on data as it becomes available, in contrast to batch learning where the entire dataset is used at once.
Physical implementation of an artificial neural network with optical components.

Process of identifying the grammatical type of words in a text.
Branch of machine learning.
Type of artificial neural network.
Innovative technique to solve partial differential equations.
Class of reinforcement learning algorithms.
Variety of statistical techniques to make predictions about future or otherwise unknown events.
Subfield of machine learning.
Statistical technique used by marketers to determine consumers’ preferred core benefits.
Quantum Machine Learning combines quantum computing and ML to enhance algorithms, leveraging unique quantum properties, like superposition and entanglement, for efficient problem-solving.
Computational neural network model based on the principles of quantum mechanics.
Research area in computer science.
An artificial neural network that uses radial basis functions as activation functions.
Artificial neural network with connections forming a hierarchical structure, processing data recursively.
Training method using human feedback to rank responses and train a reward model that improves model outputs.
Type of artificial neural network.
Regularization technique for ill-posed problems.
Machine learning for robots.
Specialized form of regression analysis, in statistics.
Machine learning methods that try to develop rules that are to be applied in particular contexts.
Machine learning technique useful for dimensionality reduction.
Computational application of concept approximation.

Regression models that combine parametric and nonparametric models.
Numeric representation of a sentence.
Use of natural language processing, text analysis and computational linguistics to identify and extract subjective information in source materials.
Family of machine learning approaches.

Function that maps a k-element real-valued vector to a k-element categorical probability distribution.
Automatic conversion of spoken language into text.
Artificial neural network that mimics real neurons.

Problem of identifying to which of a set of categories (sub-populations) a new observation belongs, on the basis of a training set of data containing observations (or instances) whose category membership is known.
Subdiscipline of artificial intelligence.
Type of artificial neural network.
Supervised machine learning techniques.
Machine learning task of learning a function that maps an input to an output based on example input-output pairs.
Set of methods for supervised statistical learning.
Mathematical activation function in data analysis.

Automatic analysis of syntactic structure of natural language.
Process of analysing text to extract information from it.
Process of dividing written text into meaningful units, such as words, sentences, or topics.
Heuristic for choosing actions that addresses the exploration-exploitation dilemma in the multi-armed bandit problem.
Multilayer artificial neural network that classifies patterns with shift-invariance and models context at each layer of the network.
Research field in deep learning.
Function for machine learning algorithms.
Machine learning technique.
Deep learning system in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive.
Machine learning algorithm for vision processing.
Machine learning approach where noisy, limited, or imprecise sources are used to provide supervision signal for labeling large amounts of training data in a supervised learning setting.
Problem setup in machine learning, where at test time, a learner observes samples from classes that were not observed during training, and needs to predict the class they belong to.
